subject: Request: special concession for Catalyst slate (VP/CFO signoff needed)
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: special concession for Catalyst slate (VP/CFO signoff needed)

Team — quick summary from this morning's call with NebulaHealth: they want to consolidate a Dedicated pool + Private VPC deployment for a multi-year pilot (12 months) and are asking for a one-time structured concession to make the economics work. Key asks: 35% first-year discount on hosted unit rates, a $50k onboarding credit, and 12 months of extended log retention on Private (they will pay for storage but want us to waive the retention surcharge).

Numbers in the attached workbook show the blended ARR and LTTV impact — baseline ARR for the pilot is $1.1M, the proposed concession would drop revenue to ~$770k in year one but increases probability to close to 90% and a multi-year expansion runway. Sales prefers to accept if we can get VP/CFO signoff for the concession and a conditional make-good clause (if usage exceeds X, we reduce concession).

Asking for: your read on business risk, whether we can approve a 35% concession or propose an alternate structure (staggered ramp, credits vs percent), and any one-off approvals we should attach. I've attached the pricing workbook and a short concession_summary.pdf.

Attachments: catalyst_pricing_workbook.xlsx (xlsx), concession_summary.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
David
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: special concession for Catalyst slate (VP/CFO signoff needed)

David — thanks for the clean packet. A few immediate thoughts:

- 35% is steep relative to our guardrails for new Dedicated accounts; I'd prefer a blended approach: 20% year one + $30k onboarding credit + a time-limited retention waiver (90 days free, then normal surcharge).
- We should tie the concession to measurable milestones (pilot go-live + 3-month usage threshold) and include a catch-up clause if they over-index on tokens.
- Legal will push for a capped make-good and a hard end date for retention waiver.

If we want to keep the 35% number, we need CFO buy-in on the revenue trade-off and a clear expansion plan. I'm happy to join a short alignment call with Finance to present the business case.

-Markissa
VP, Sales Operations

On 2026-11-17 08:12, David Kim wrote:
> Team — quick summary from this morning's call with NebulaHealth: they want to consolidate a Dedicated pool + Private VPC deployment for a multi-year pilot (12 months) and are asking for a one-time structured concession to make the economics work...

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: special concession for Catalyst slate (VP/CFO signoff needed)

Agree with Marissa. We shouldn't set a precedent with 35% off list for year one unless there are contractual guardrails and an explicit expansion milestone. Mina — can you weigh in on whether Finance is comfortable with a 20% blended concession + $30k onboarding credit as a fallback? If it's defensible from a revenue protection standpoint, we can offer the 20% + credits today and reserve the 35% only for a fully committed multi-year (36mo) purchase.

Thoughts on the retention ask: technically straightforward for their Private deployment, but we need to capture the incremental storage cost and formalize the retention waiver in SOW (time-bound).

-Markus
Chief Commercial Officer

On 2026-11-17 10:03, Marissa Cole wrote:
> David — thanks for the clean packet. A few immediate thoughts...

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@nebulahealth.com>, Alex Lopez <alex.lopez@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: special concession for Catalyst slate (VP/CFO signoff needed)

Sam — following internal alignment, we'd like to propose an updated concession structure that is faster for approval and keeps the pilot economics healthy for us while addressing your team's deployment concerns.

Proposed (fast-approval):
- 20% discount on unit rates for year one (applied to Dedicated + Private billable units)
- $30,000 onboarding credit (applied to month 1 invoice)
- Retention surcharge waived for first 90 days on Private; thereafter normal surcharge applies
- Conditional upsell clause: if NebulaHealth commits to a 24-month extension within the pilot, Redwood will apply a retroactive bill credit to reach an effective 30% first-year discount (caps and thresholds in attached draft SOW)

We think this hits both objectives: quicker internal signoff and a clear path for you to get additional savings tied to commitment. Attached is a short draft SOW (nebula_sow_draft.docx) showing the clause. Please let me know if this is acceptable or if you need the original 35% commitment to move forward.

Attachments: nebula_sow_draft.docx (docx)

Thanks,
David

On 2026-11-17 12:45, Markus Klein wrote:
> Agree with Marissa. We shouldn't set a precedent with 35% off list for year one...

From: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@nebulahealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Lopez <alex.lopez@nebulahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:08:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: special concession for Catalyst slate (VP/CFO signoff needed)

David — appreciate the quick follow-up and the revised structure. The Nebula execs discussed; they're willing to accept the 20% + $30k onboarding credit as long as: (1) the 90-day retention waiver is in writing, (2) the conditional upsell clause to reach 30% is clearly defined, and (3) we have a path to a search-and-run SLA for Dedicated that matches expected QPS.

I'm attaching our internal redlines (summary inline): retention waiver must be 120 days (not 90), and the retro credit should be applied at the close of the 6th month if we commit to 24 months. If those two changes are acceptable, we can sign the SOW next week and expedite procurement.

Best,
Sam Reynolds
Director of Platform Operations
NebulaHealth

Attachments referenced: nebula_redlines_summary.pdf

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: special concession for Catalyst slate (VP/CFO signoff needed)

Markus / team — reviewed the model and legal guardrails. Finance can sign off on the 20% + $30k onboarding credit with the following binding conditions:

1) Retention waiver: 120 days confirmed (we'll accept Nebula's ask) but storage overages are tracked and invoiced monthly after the waiver period.
2) Retro credit mechanics: if Nebula executes a 24-month commitment before month 6, apply a retroactive bill credit at month 6 to reach an effective 30% first-year discount (credit capped at $200k).
3) SLA: technical SLA for Dedicated must be in a separate SOW appendix; engineering will sign off on QPS targets prior to contract signature.

Please update the SOW to reflect the retention waiver length and the retro credit cap. Once legal signs off on the final wording, Finance will issue the approval memo for execution.

I've attached a short approval note (concession_summary.pdf) for the contract folder.

-Mina
CFO (interim)
Redwood Inference
